results.title: Linear bound on the prime divisors of a finite soluble group (Kourovka 14.66)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement, posed by A. Moretó, that there are natural numbers $a$ and $b$ such that for every finite soluble group $G$ and every natural number $m$, if the order of every element of $G$ has at most $m$ distinct prime divisors, then $|G|$ has at most $am + b$ distinct prime divisors.

results.title: Finite soluble groups satisfy a linear prime-divisor bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There are natural numbers $a$ and $b$ such that for every finite soluble group $G$ and every natural number $m$, if the order of every element of $G$ has at most $m$ distinct prime divisors, then $|G|$ has at most $am + b$ distinct prime divisors. That is, Kourovka Problem 14.66 has a positive answer.

results.title: Injectivity of an operator on the orthogonal complement of its kernel
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two points of `(ker B)ᗮ` with the same image under `B` are equal, since their difference lies in `ker B ∩ (ker B)ᗮ`.

results.title: Preimages in the orthogonal complement of the kernel under range inclusion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `A.range ≤ B.range`, every `A x` has a preimage under `B` in `(ker B)ᗮ`.

results.title: Underlying function of the Douglas factor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The underlying function of the canonical factor: the chosen preimage of `A x` in `(ker B)ᗮ`.

results.title: Defining properties of the Douglas preimage
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The defining properties of the chosen preimage.

results.title: Douglas factor as a linear map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The canonical factor as a linear map.

results.title: Continuity of the Douglas factor via the closed graph theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The canonical factor is continuous, by the (sequential) closed graph theorem: if `u n → x` and `C (u n) → y`, then `y ∈ (ker B)ᗮ` (the orthogonal complement is closed) and `B y = A x` (continuity of `A` and `B`), so `y = C x` by uniqueness of the preimage in `(ker B)ᗮ`.

results.title: Canonical factor in Douglas' lemma
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The canonical factor in Douglas' lemma: for `x : E`, the unique element of `(ker B)ᗮ` mapped by `B` to `A x`.

results.title: Douglas factor takes values in the kernel's orthogonal complement
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The canonical factor lands in `(ker B)ᗮ`.

results.title: Douglas factor gives a preimage under B
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The canonical factor is a preimage: `B (C x) = A x`.

results.title: Douglas factor factors A through B
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The canonical factor factors `A` through `B`.

results.title: Uniqueness of the Douglas factor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The canonical factor is the unique operator with the two defining properties.

results.title: Douglas' lemma: range inclusion iff factorization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Douglas' lemma, range form: `A.range ≤ B.range` iff `A = B ∘L C` for some bounded `C`.

results.title: Factorization implies majorization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `A = B ∘L C`, then majorization holds with constant `‖C‖`.

results.title: Douglas' lemma: majorization gives a norm-bounded factor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Douglas' lemma, factorization form with a norm bound: majorization with constant `c` yields a factor `C` with `A = B ∘L C` and `‖C‖ ≤ c`.

results.title: Douglas' lemma: majorization iff factorization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Douglas' lemma, majorization form: majorization holds iff `A` factors through `B`.

results.title: Douglas' lemma: range inclusion iff majorization
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Douglas' lemma, range/majorization form: `A.range ≤ B.range` iff majorization holds.

results.title: The square test function

results.title: The shifted square
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $x \in [0, 1]$, the function $y \mapsto (y - x)^2$ on $[0, 1]$, as an element of $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$.

results.title: Expansion of the shifted square
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Write $e(y) = y$ and $q(y) = y^2$ for the identity and square functions and $1$ for the constant function one, as elements of $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$. For every $x \in [0, 1]$, the function $y \mapsto (y - x)^2$ in $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ equals $q - 2x \cdot e + x^2 \cdot 1$.

results.title: Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a sequence $(u_n)$ in $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ converges to $e$ in the sup norm, then $u_n(x) \to e(x)$ for every $x \in [0, 1]$.

results.title: Positive linear operators are monotone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a real-linear operator on $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ that is positive: $(L f)(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in [0, 1]$ whenever $f(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in [0, 1]$. If $g, h \in C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ satisfy $g(x) \le h(x)$ for all $x \in [0, 1]$, then $(L g)(x) \le (L h)(x)$ for every $x \in [0, 1]$.

results.title: Positive linear operators bound absolute values
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ be a real-linear operator on $C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ that is positive: $(L f)(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in [0, 1]$ whenever $f(x) \ge 0$ for all $x \in [0, 1]$. If $g, h \in C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ satisfy $|g(y)| \le h(y)$ for all $y \in [0, 1]$, then $|(L g)(x)| \le (L h)(x)$ for every $x \in [0, 1]$.

results.title: Quadratic bound from a modulus of continuity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \in C([0, 1], \mathbb{R})$ have sup norm $\|f\|$, let $x \in [0, 1]$, and let $\delta > 0$, $\varepsilon \ge 0$ and $C \ge 0$ be real numbers with $2\|f\| \le C \delta^2$. If $|f(y) - f(x)| < \varepsilon$ for every $y \in [0, 1]$ with $|y - x| < \delta$, then $|f(y) - f(x)| \le \varepsilon + C (y - x)^2$ for every $y \in [0, 1]$.

results.title: Congruent plane sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two sets $E$ and $F$ in the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ are congruent when some isometry of the plane onto itself maps $E$ onto $F$.

results.title: Congruence-invariant set functions on the plane
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $\mu$ that assigns to every subset of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ a value in $[0, \infty]$ is congruence invariant when $\mu(E) = \mu(F)$ for all congruent plane sets $E$ and $F$.

results.title: Weak Sidon set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a *weak Sidon set* (or *well spread*) if sums of two distinct elements of $A$ are distinct: whenever $a, b, c, d \in A$ satisfy $a < b$, $c < d$ and $a + b = c + d$, then $a = c$.

results.title: Sidon sets are weak Sidon sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is a weak Sidon set.

results.title: Ideal generated by a property
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $P$ be a property of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$. The ideal generated by $P$ is the family of all sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that are contained in the union of finitely many sets with property $P$. The empty union is allowed, so the empty set always belongs to it.

results.title: Sets with a property lie in the ideal it generates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a property of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$. Every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with property $P$ lies in the ideal generated by $P$, the family of all subsets of finite unions of sets with property $P$.

results.title: Generated ideals are closed under subsets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a property of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$. If $A$ lies in the ideal generated by $P$ and $B \subseteq A$, then $B$ also lies in the ideal generated by $P$.

results.title: Generated ideals are closed under unions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a property of subsets of $\mathbb{N}$, and consider the ideal generated by $P$, the family of all subsets of finite unions of sets with property $P$. If $A$ and $B$ lie in this ideal, then so does $A \cup B$.

results.title: Sidon ideal
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The Sidon ideal $\mathrm{Si}$ is the ideal on $\mathbb{N}$ generated by the Sidon sets: it consists of all sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ contained in a finite union of Sidon subsets of $\mathbb{N}$.

results.title: Gap-lacunary set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is *gap-lacunary* (called *lacunary* in the source) if it is infinite and, writing $A(n)$ for its $n$-th element in increasing order (counting from $n = 0$), the gaps $A(n+1) - A(n)$ tend to infinity as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Gap-lacunary sets are infinite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every gap-lacunary set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is infinite.

results.title: Almost thin set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is *almost thin* if it is infinite and, writing $A(n)$ for its $n$-th element in increasing order (counting from $n = 0$), there is a real number $\alpha < 1$ such that $A(n)/A(n+1) \le \alpha$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

results.title: Almost thin sets are infinite
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every almost thin set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is infinite.

results.title: Van der Waerden ideal
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The van der Waerden ideal $W$ consists of the sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ for which there is an $n > 0$ such that $A$ contains no arithmetic progression $a, a + r, \dots, a + (n - 1) r$ of $n$ terms with $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and $r > 0$.

results.title: The empty set lies in the van der Waerden ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The empty subset of $\mathbb{N}$ belongs to the van der Waerden ideal.

results.title: Positive difference set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $Z \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, the positive difference set $D(Z)$ is the set of all differences $a - b$ with $a, b \in Z$ and $a > b$.

results.title: The ideal of sets avoiding large difference sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $Z \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, let $D(Z) = \{a - b : a, b \in Z,\ b < a\}$ be its set of positive differences. The ideal $D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ consists of the sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ for which there is a natural number $n$ such that $D(Z) \not\subseteq A$ for every $n$-element set $Z \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.

results.title: The empty set lies in the difference-set ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The empty set belongs to the ideal $D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ of sets $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ for which some natural number $n$ satisfies $D(Z) \not\subseteq A$ for every $n$-element set $Z \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, where $D(Z)$ is the set of positive differences $a - b$ with $a, b \in Z$ and $b < a$.

results.title: Block sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $C$, $M$ and $K$, the block $\mathrm{Block}(n, C, M, K)$ is the set of natural numbers $M l + C \cdot 2^k$ with $0 \le k < n$ and $1 \le l \le K$.

results.title: One-term blocks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $C$ and $M$, the block $\mathrm{Block}(1, C, M, 1) = \{M l + C \cdot 2^k : 0 \le k < 1,\ 1 \le l \le 1\}$ is the singleton $\{M + C\}$.

results.title: Weak Sidon sets split into two Sidon sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every weak Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is the union of two disjoint Sidon sets $B$ and $C$.

results.title: Weak Sidon sets generate the Sidon ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The ideal on $\mathbb{N}$ generated by the weak Sidon sets equals the Sidon ideal.

results.title: The Sidon ideal is $F_\sigma$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Give the Cantor space $\{0, 1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ the product topology and identify each set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with its indicator function. Then the set of indicator functions of the members of the Sidon ideal is a countable union of closed subsets of $\{0, 1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$.

results.title: Positive sets whose elements at least double are Sidon
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with $0 \notin A$, and write $A(n)$ for the $n$-th element of $A$ in increasing order, counting from $n = 0$, with $A(n) = 0$ when $A$ has at most $n$ elements. If $2 A(n) \le A(n+1)$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, then $A$ is a Sidon set.

results.title: The Sidon ideal is contained in the lacunary ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Call a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ lacunary if it is infinite and the gaps $A(n + 1) - A(n)$ between consecutive elements tend to infinity, where $A(n)$ is the $n$-th element of $A$ in increasing order. Every set in the Sidon ideal is contained in a finite union of lacunary sets, that is, it lies in the ideal $\mathrm{Lac}$ generated by the lacunary sets.

results.title: Mian–Chowla lower bound for an infinite Sidon set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and a real constant $c > 0$ such that $|A \cap \{1, \dots, n\}| > c\, n^{1/3}$ for every natural number $n \ge 1$.

results.title: Ajtai–Komlós–Szemerédi lower bound for an infinite Sidon set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ and a real constant $c > 0$ such that $|A \cap \{1, \dots, n\}| > c\, (n \log n)^{1/3}$ for every natural number $n \ge 1$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm.

results.title: Ruzsa's lower bound for an infinite Sidon set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ such that for every real $\varepsilon > 0$, the inequality $|A \cap \{1, \dots, n\}| > n^{\sqrt{2} - 1 - \varepsilon}$ holds for all sufficiently large natural numbers $n$; that is, $|A \cap \{1, \dots, n\}| > n^{\sqrt{2} - 1 - o(1)}$.

results.title: A Sidon set outside the almost thin ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a Sidon set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that is not contained in any finite union of almost thin sets; that is, $A$ does not belong to the ideal generated by the almost thin sets.

results.title: The almost thin ideal is contained in the Sidon ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that is contained in a finite union of almost thin sets is contained in a finite union of Sidon sets; that is, the ideal generated by the almost thin sets is contained in the Sidon ideal.

results.title: A block not covered by few Sidon sets
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and $C \ge 1$ be natural numbers, and put $M = C \cdot 2^n + 1$ and $K = (n - 1)\binom{n}{2} + 1$. Then the block $\mathrm{Block}(n, C, M, K) = \{M l + C \cdot 2^k : 0 \le k < n,\ 1 \le l \le K\}$ is not contained in the union of any $n - 1$ Sidon subsets of $\mathbb{N}$.

results.title: A set in the van der Waerden, lacunary and difference-set ideals outside the Sidon ideal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There is a set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ that belongs to the van der Waerden ideal, is contained in a finite union of gap-lacunary sets (infinite sets whose gaps between consecutive elements tend to infinity), and belongs to the ideal $D_{\mathrm{fin}}$ of sets avoiding large difference sets, but is not contained in any finite union of Sidon sets.

results.title: Gessel alphabet
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Gessel alphabet over $S = [n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ is the disjoint union of an unbarred copy and a barred copy of $[n]$: it has an unbarred letter $i$ and a barred letter $\bar{i}$ for each $i \in [n]$.

results.title: Unbarred occurrences of a label
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a word (a finite sequence of letters) over the Gessel alphabet over $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ and let $m$ be a natural number. The unbarred count of $m$ in $w$ is the number of positions of $w$ that hold the unbarred letter $m$; it is $0$ when $m \notin [n]$.

results.title: Barred occurrences of a label
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a word (a finite sequence of letters) over the Gessel alphabet over $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ and let $m$ be a natural number. The barred count of $m$ in $w$ is the number of positions of $w$ that hold the barred letter $\bar{m}$; it is $0$ when $m \notin [n]$.

results.title: Signed balance of a label
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $w$ be a word over the Gessel alphabet over $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ and let $m$ be a natural number. The signed balance of $m$ in $w$ is the integer obtained by subtracting the number of occurrences of the barred letter $\bar{m}$ in $w$ from the number of occurrences of the unbarred letter $m$ in $w$; it is $0$ when $m \notin [n]$.

results.title: Gessel word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number. For a word $u$ over the Gessel alphabet over $S = [n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ and a natural number $m$, write $\beta_u(m)$ for the signed balance of $m$ in $u$: the number of occurrences of the unbarred letter $m$ in $u$ minus the number of occurrences of the barred letter $\bar{m}$ in $u$. A word $w$ over this alphabet is a Gessel word when, for every prefix $w'$ of $w$ (including the empty…

results.title: Complete Gessel words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A word $w$ over the Gessel alphabet of $S = [n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ is a complete Gessel word when it is a Gessel word and, for every $m \in [n]$, the unbarred letter $m$ and the barred letter $\bar m$ occur the same number of times in $w$.

results.title: Complete Gessel words are the Gessel words of zero balance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A word $w$ over the Gessel alphabet of $[n] = \{1, \dots, n\}$ is a complete Gessel word if and only if it is a Gessel word and, for every $m \in [n]$, the signed balance of $m$ in $w$ (the number of occurrences of the unbarred letter $m$ minus the number of occurrences of the barred letter $\bar m$) is zero.

results.title: Dyck paths of semilength 3 with two peaks
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With one color for every block ($\gamma_j = 1$ for all $j$), the number of colored Dyck paths of semilength $3$ with $2$ peaks is $d_{3,2}(\gamma) = 3$, a Narayana number.

results.title: Diagonals of a convex polygon
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, label the vertices of the convex $(n+2)$-gon $0, 1, \dots, n+1$ in cyclic order. Its diagonals are the pairs $(a, b)$ of natural numbers with $a + 2 \le b \le n + 1$ and $(a, b) \ne (0, n+1)$; the excluded pair is the side joining the vertices $0$ and $n+1$.

results.title: Noncrossing sets of diagonals
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Reachability in a labelled transition system is transitive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: In a labelled transition system, say that a state $s$ can reach a state $t$ when there is a finite list of labels along which $s$ makes a multistep transition to $t$. If $s$ can reach $m$ and $m$ can reach $t$, then $s$ can reach $t$.

results.title: Shifted sequence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ and a natural number $k$, the shift of the sequence by $k$ is the sequence whose $i$-th term is $s_{i+k}$; that is, the suffix starting at index $k$, re-indexed from $0$.

results.title: Finite run
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In a labelled transition system, a sequence of states $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ is a finite run of length $k$ when for every $i < k$ there is a label $a$ such that there is a transition from $s_i$ to $s_{i+1}$ labelled $a$.

results.title: Infinite run
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: In a labelled transition system, a sequence of states $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ is an infinite run when for every $i$ there is a label $a$ such that there is a transition from $s_i$ to $s_{i+1}$ labelled $a$.

results.title: Invariant principle for infinite runs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $P$ be a predicate on the states of a labelled transition system such that, whenever $P(s)$ holds and there is a transition from $s$ to $t$ with some label, $P(t)$ holds. Then for every infinite run $s_0, s_1, s_2, \dots$ with $P(s_0)$, the predicate $P(s_k)$ holds for every $k$.

results.title: Adjacent comparator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n$ wires and an index $i$, this is the comparator on wires $i$ and $i + 1$ when $i + 1 < n$, and nothing when wire $i + 1$ does not exist.

results.title: Bubble pass
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: On $n$ wires, the bubble pass ending at wire $m$ is the comparator network $(0, 1), (1, 2), \ldots, (m - 1, m)$, applied in this order, where a comparator $(i, i + 1)$ is left out when wire $i + 1$ does not exist (that is, when $i + 1 \ge n$).

results.title: Successive bubble passes
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: On $n$ wires and for a number $m$, this is the comparator network obtained by concatenating the bubble passes ending at wires $m - 1, m - 2, \ldots, 0$, in this order; for $m = 0$ it is empty.

results.title: Bubble sorting network
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The bubble sorting network on $n$ wires is the comparator network obtained by concatenating the bubble passes ending at wires $n - 1, n - 2, \ldots, 0$, in this order, where the bubble pass ending at wire $k$ consists of the comparators $(0, 1), (1, 2), \ldots, (k - 1, k)$.

results.title: Effect of one bubble pass
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $w$ be an input on $n$ wires with values in a linearly ordered type, let $m < n$, and let $w'$ be the output of the bubble pass ending at wire $m$ (the comparators $(0, 1), \ldots, (m - 1, m)$) run on $w$. Then $w'_i = w_i$ for every wire $i > m$; $w'_i \le w'_m$ for every wire $i \le m$; and for every wire $i \le m$ there is a wire $j \le m$ with $w'_i = w_j$.

results.title: Settled top wires
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $w$ assign to each of $n$ wires a value in a linearly ordered type, and let $m$ be a natural number. Then $w$ is settled from $m$ when $w_i \le w_j$ for all wires $m \le i \le j$ (the wires $m, \ldots, n - 1$ are sorted) and $w_i \le w_j$ for all wires $i < m \le j$ (they hold the largest values). This is the invariant before the bubble pass ending at wire $m - 1$.

results.title: The bubble network sorts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The bubble network sorts every input over every linear order.

results.title: Size of a bubble pass
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On $n$ wires, for every $m < n$ the bubble pass ending at wire $m$ has exactly $m$ comparators.

results.title: Size of the bubble sorting network
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$, the bubble sorting network on $n$ wires has $n(n - 1)/2$ comparators: twice its number of comparators is $n(n - 1)$.
